source_text: Critics of preservation arguments, including some indigenous health advocates, point to declining voluntary participation—evident in surveys from Arnhem Land communities by the 2000s—attributable to awareness of health detriments and shifting generational values, suggesting adaptation through symbolic proxies rather than physical enactment preserves essence without injury. [40]
